Shows your **Picnic** grocery deliveries in Gladys (Netherlands, Germany,
Belgium, France), read only: the slot of the next delivery, its estimated
arrival when Picnic gives one, the order cut-off, the status of the last
order, and the cart. A scene trigger fires when the delivery is approaching.

> **Unofficial API, never tested with a real account.** The integration
> talks to the API of the Picnic app, which Picnic does not document and may
> change at any time. It was written from python-picnic-api2 and the Home
> Assistant integration, and tested against made-up answers only. Not
> affiliated with Picnic.

## What you get

One device, **Picnic**, with these features (all read only):

| Feature                          | Example                              | Notes                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Next delivery: slot start        | `2026-10-18 14:15`                   | local time given by Picnic; `—` without a planned delivery   |
| Next delivery: slot end          | `2026-10-18 16:15`                   |                                                              |
| Next delivery: estimated arrival | `2026-10-18 14:48 (14:40–15:00)`     | only when Picnic gives an ETA (usually on the day), else `—` |
| Order before                     | `2026-10-17 23:00`                   | see below                                                    |
| Last order status                | `Upcoming`, `Delivered`, `Cancelled` | other statuses shown as Picnic sends them                    |
| Cart: articles                   | `3`                                  |                                                              |
| Cart: total                      | `12.34` €                            |                                                              |

**Order before** is the cut-off of the booked delivery while it can still be
changed; once it has passed, the cut-off of the slot selected in the cart,
else of the first slot the cart offers.

Gladys has no date feature: times are text, shown as the local time Picnic
sends (the time zone of your Picnic country).

Nothing is ever added to the cart or ordered: this version only reads.

## Set up

1. In Gladys, install the **Picnic** integration from the store.
2. Enter the **e-mail** and **password** of your Picnic account (the ones of
   the app) and choose its **country**, then save.
3. If the status asks for a verification code, see below.
4. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the **Picnic** device.

The password field is a `secret` field: Gladys keeps it in its database
(in plain text, like every configuration value, and in its backups), never
shows it again, and the integration only sends it to Picnic, as the MD5
digest the Picnic app sends.

### Verification code (two steps)

For a new sign-in, Picnic may ask for a code sent by SMS or e-mail. The
integration never asks for one by itself (no SMS without your click). When
the status says "Picnic asks for a verification code":

1. In the configuration screen, under **Send the verification code**,
   choose **SMS** or **E-mail** and click the button. The integration signs
   in and Picnic sends the code.
2. Under **Verify the code**, type the code you received and click the
   button. "Code accepted" means connected.

The session is then kept (in the integration's `/data`): no code at the next
restarts. Picnic may still ask for a code again later, when the session
expires or is revoked (a new device, a password change): the status then
says so, and the same two steps apply.

- A code is requested at most once a minute (even across a restart).
- Clicking **Send the verification code** more than 10 minutes after the
  sign-in that asked for it signs in again first (one sign-in), then asks
  for the code: use the newest code you receive.
- While connected, **Send the verification code** answers "already
  connected" and sends nothing.
- If Picnic refuses to send the code, the message gives its reason code: try
  the other channel, or later. If the code is refused, check it or ask for a
  new one. A restart between the two steps loses nothing.

## Refresh

- Every **15 minutes** by default (5 to 60, _Refresh interval_). Each read
  is 2 requests: the cart and the delivery list.
- **Delivery day**: from 12 hours before the slot, every 5 minutes.
- **Around the delivery**: from 45 minutes before the slot (or the ETA) to
  30 minutes after it, every 2 minutes, plus the live position (a third
  request, for the ETA).

## Scene trigger: "Picnic delivery approaching"

Fires **once per delivery**, when the estimated arrival given by Picnic is at
most _"Delivery approaching" lead_ minutes away (15 by default, 5 to 60).
Without an ETA from Picnic, it does not fire. Variables:
`minutes` (minutes before the arrival), `eta`, `slot_start`, `slot_end`
(local times as text). Example: switch the porch light on and send a message
"Picnic in 15 minutes".

## When things go wrong

- **E-mail or password refused**: the integration stops and waits. Check the
  e-mail, the password and the country, then save (or click _Test the
  connection_). It never signs in again by itself after a refusal.
- **Session refused**: the session token kept is refused, the integration
  signs in again **once**; refused again, it pauses with a message and tries
  again (one sign-in each time) after 1 hour, 6 hours, then every 24 hours.
  If such a try is refused or asks for a code, it stops as above (it never
  requests a code by itself). _Test the connection_ tries at once.
- **Sign-in request rejected (HTTP 400)**: Picnic has probably changed its
  API; the integration stops and asks to update it.
- **Too many requests (429)**: a pause of 1 minute to 6 hours (Picnic's
  `Retry-After`, 15 minutes without it), for every read and button, kept
  across a restart and a change of account. **HTTP 403** (a block): one hour,
  for every read and button too.
- _Test the connection_ reads at most once every 30 seconds (one sign-in at
  most), without the live position, so it answers within a minute.
- **Picnic unavailable (5xx, network)**: new tries after 2, 5, 10, 15, then
  every 30 minutes.
- The live position failing never hides the cart and the deliveries.

## Limits

- Unofficial API: Picnic may change it, block it or ask for more checks.
- Read only: no cart changes, no ordering (maybe later).
- One Picnic account per Gladys.
- Never tested with a real account: please report what you see on the
  [GitHub repository](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-picnic/issues)
  (without your e-mail, password or codes).

## Privacy

The integration keeps in `/data/picnic-state.json` (readable by its
container only): a random device id, the session token, the account it
belongs to as a hash of the e-mail and the country, your Picnic user id (it
names the Gladys device), the end of a 429 pause, when a code was last
requested, and the ids of the deliveries already announced. Neither the e-mail nor the password. Nothing
is sent anywhere but to Picnic.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Picnic asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Picnic account | `section` | No | Shows your Picnic deliveries in Gladys, read only: start and end of the next delivery slot, its estimated arrival when Picnic gives one, the order cut-off, the status of the last order, the number of articles and the total of the cart, and a scene trigger when the delivery is approaching. Enter the e-mail, password and country of the Picnic app, save, then add the Picnic device from the Discovery tab. If Picnic asks for a verification code, use the two buttons below: send the code, then type it in. Read every 15 minutes, more often on delivery day. Unofficial API, never tested with a real account. Not affiliated with Picnic. |
| Picnic e-mail | `string` | Yes |  |
| Picnic password | `secret` | Yes | Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to Picnic (as the MD5 digest the app sends). |
| Country of the account | `select` | Yes |  |
| Refresh interval (min) | `number` | No | Minutes between two reads (5 to 60). On delivery day, every 5 minutes, then every 2 minutes around the delivery. |
| "Delivery approaching" lead (min) | `number` | No | The scene trigger fires once per delivery, this many minutes before the estimated arrival (5 to 60), when Picnic gives one. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the feature names of the device added from now on, and for the order statuses. |

## How to install Picnic in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Picnic appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-picnic:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-picnic](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-picnic).

Picnic requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Picnic is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core.
